description:
Non-required nits and improvements surfaced by the code review of
explorer-align-ranking-metric-with-tpc-standards.  No Required issues
were found in that review; this item tracks the three nit/consider findings.

anti_patterns.dont: change the sort logic in w1

preserves.behavior: QueryHeatmap sort behavior - only the aria-sort attribute changes in w1
showGeomeanCol behavior for all current benchmarks - equivalent semantics, just a less fragile guard

verifications.description: QueryHeatmap axe test passes with correct aria-sort
verifications.expected: no axe violations, all tests pass

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run typecheck && npm test

work_units.notes:
QueryHeatmap.tsx:197 - `aria-sort="none"` is used on the primary metric
column header, but the table IS sorted by that column (lines 94-103 sort
`sorted` by primary metric).  Screen readers announce "sort: none" which
is incorrect.

Fix: set `aria-sort` dynamically based on sort direction:
  aria-sort={higherIsBetter ? "descending" : "ascending"}

The query-timing columns (Q1, Q2, …) correctly retain aria-sort="none"
since those columns are not sorted.
work_units.summary: Fix aria-sort on primary metric column in QueryHeatmap

work_units.notes:
QueryHeatmap.tsx:164 -
  const showGeomeanCol = primaryMetric === "power_score";

This hardcodes the assumption that the secondary column is always
display_geomean_ms when primary is power_score.  The artifact already
carries `ranking?.secondary_metric`.  A more robust guard:
  const showGeomeanCol = primaryMetric !== "display_geomean_ms";
or use `ranking?.secondary_metric === "display_geomean_ms"`.

Functionally equivalent for all current benchmark families, but less
fragile if a future family uses a different metric pair.
work_units.summary: Use ranking?.secondary_metric to gate the secondary geomean column

work_units.notes:
ranking.test.ts pins all 9 known benchmark→metric mappings explicitly.
Like chartRegistry.meta.test.ts, it protects against TS-side drift but
not Python-side drift - if a 10th family is added to models.py without
updating the test, no CI failure occurs.

The existing comment already says "When you add a new benchmark to the
Python registry, add a case here too."  This work item is to add a note
explaining WHY (the test cannot parse Python source) so maintainers
understand the limitation rather than assuming the test is comprehensive.
If w4 from explorer-chart-coverage-review-followups adopts a dynamic
parse approach for chartRegistry, mirror that approach here.
work_units.summary: Add comment to ranking.test.ts clarifying triple-write limitation
